description: We are alishkaTeam, a team participating in NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. Our goal is to solve real-world and space exploration problems using NASA open data, AI, and innovative technologies. We prioritize scientific accuracy, strong architecture, and practical solutions. We welcome motivated teammates interested in Python, machine learning, data science, web development, and space research. We value creativity, teamwork, and critical thinking.
summary:
EARTH SENSES is a multilingual web application that investigates climate trends and relationships using real NASA POWER and MERRA-2 data. Users select a location, variables, and time period to explore temperature, humidity, and precipitation through interactive maps, charts, statistical tests, and evidence records.

Unlike a conventional climate dashboard, the system checks whether apparent relationships are driven by seasonal cycles, whether trends remain statistically reliable, and whether conclusions change when the analysis period changes.

Our case study in Pavlodar, Kazakhstan, reveals a striking result: the correlation between precipitation and relative humidity changes from −0.28 in raw monthly data to +0.59 after removing seasonal effects.

Every finding includes uncertainty, counterevidence, limitations, and traceable NASA data sources. By helping people distinguish meaningful patterns from misleading correlations, EARTH SENSES supports climate education, scientific reasoning, and responsible interpretation of Earth-system data.
details:
EARTH SENSES — Interconnected Earth Intelligence

https://earth-senses.vercel.app/

The Problem

NASA provides valuable Earth-observation and climate datasets, but interpreting them correctly remains challenging. Seasonal cycles can create misleading correlations, statistical significance may depend on the selected years, and relationships between variables can be mistaken for causal effects.

Our Solution

EARTH SENSES is an interactive web application designed to investigate, verify, and explain patterns in Earth's climate system.

Users choose a geographic location, select environmental variables, and define an observation period. The application retrieves or loads NASA POWER data based on MERRA-2 reanalysis and performs statistical investigations.

Its main capabilities include:

  • Trend Analysis: Theil–Sen trend estimates, confidence intervals, statistical significance tests, and corrections for autocorrelation and multiple comparisons.
  • Relationship Analysis: Correlations before and after removing seasonality, partial correlations, time-lag analysis, and checks for relationships caused by how variables are calculated.
  • Evidence Records: Each finding includes supporting evidence, counterevidence, methodological details, limitations, and a SHA-256 fingerprint of its source NASA data.
  • Interactive Exploration: Geographic maps, climate graphs, relationship networks, regional comparisons, and downloadable reports.
  • Multilingual Interface: English, Kazakh, and Russian, with an interactive 3D Earth introduction.

Scientific Demonstration

We investigated precipitation and relative humidity in Pavlodar, Kazakhstan, using monthly NASA POWER/MERRA-2 data for 2001–2024.

The raw correlation was −0.28. After removing average seasonal cycles, the correlation became +0.59. This reveals how seasonal patterns can reverse the apparent interpretation of environmental relationships.

The application also identifies limitations: the association varies by season, all variables originate from one reanalysis product, and correlation alone does not establish causation.

Technology

The analytical backend was developed using Python 3.13, FastAPI, NumPy, pandas, SciPy, and statsmodels. The frontend uses React, TypeScript, Vite, MapLibre GL JS, Apache ECharts, and three.js. NASA POWER provides the main environmental data, while NASA Earth imagery supports the 3D visualization.

Automated testing and documented provenance help make the calculations reproducible.

Innovation and Impact

Our approach emphasizes evidence-based investigation rather than presenting isolated charts or statistics. The system actively tests the reliability of apparent patterns and explains what conclusions the data do and do not support.

EARTH SENSES can help students, teachers, researchers, journalists, and the public understand climate data more critically. Its educational potential lies in making scientific uncertainty and reproducibility visible and understandable.

The current version is a functional research prototype. Independent observational validation and human scientific review remain future priorities.
